episodes.165643: A line of thunderstorms produced brief gusty winds of 30-40 mph, with localized higher gusts of 40-50 mph.  One such surge of wind knocked down power poles in west central Madison County.
episodes.165647: A cold front pushed into an unseasonably warm and humid airmass over central Pennsylvania during the afternoon and early evening hours of March 7, 2022. A narrow band of gusty rain showers accompanied the front, with very little lightning observed. This line of convective showers (and isolated thunder) produced sporadic wind damage as it pushed eastward across the area.
episodes.165652: Showers and thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front produced localized strong winds and flooding.
episodes.165654: Showers and thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front produced localized strong winds and flooding.
episodes.165657: A meandering frontal boundary slowly advanced northward in the early pre-dawn hours on March 7th.  This brought a near-record moist environment and adequate instability across southern central Indiana, which combined with a low level jet stream from the southwest to produce an eastward advancing line of thunderstorms with locally severe winds. Damage was most severe in Sullivan, Shelby and Jackson Counties where winds likely gusted to 90-100 mph amid small downbursts.  Insufficient evidence was present to suggest any tornadoes occurred.
episodes.165663: Isolated severe storms produced hail, wind and heavy rain which caused localized flooding.
episodes.165664: Isolated severe storms produced hail and damaging winds.
episodes.165699: A strong cold front produced a line of low-topped showers and squalls that resulted in isolated severe wind gusts and tree and power line damage.
episodes.165863: Showers out ahead of a cold front moved into the Ohio Valley on the morning of March 6th. This cold front stalled along the western portion of the area during the afternoon. An axis of showers and a few thunderstorms set up along central and northern West Virginia ahead of this front. Moderate to heavy rain occurred at times, with some areas receiving multiple rain showers by that evening as a warm front lifted from the south, interacting with the stalled cold front. A few instances of high water over roads occurred throughout Kanawha County due to these repetitive rain showers.||A few instances of strong wind gusts also occurred throughout West Virginia during the afternoon of March 7th as a second cold front crossed through the area during the day. A few trees and some power lines were blown down by these gusty winds.
episodes.165864: Showers out ahead of a cold front moved into the Ohio Valley on the morning of March 6th. This cold front stalled along the western portion of the area during the afternoon, and an axis of showers and a few thunderstorms set up along portions of northeast Kentucky. A warm front then lifted from the south during the evening of March 6th, allowing for additional shower activity as the warm front interacted with the stalled cold front. These repetitive showers primed the area for the next day, as another cold front approached the region from the west on March 7th, bringing more showers to the area. As this band of showers ahead of the cold front pushed through the area, occasional pockets of heavier rainfall spurred on a few flooding issues in portions of northeast Kentucky as high water flowed over a few roads.
episodes.165966: A cold front passed through Central New York during the afternoon and evening hours, triggering thunderstorms. Many of these storms became severe with winds being the main threat. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down by these storms. There was also minor damage to personal property.
episodes.166336: A cold front passed through Northeastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening hours, triggering thunderstorms. Many of these storms became severe with winds being the main threat. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down by these storms.
episodes.166354: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Oklahoma during the late afternoon and evening hours of the 6th, as a strong upper level disturbance translated into the Southern Plains. The strongest thunderstorms produced hail up to quarter size.
episodes.166355: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the late afternoon and evening hours of the 6th, as a strong upper level disturbance translated into the Southern Plains. The strongest thunderstorms produced hail up to quarter size.
episodes.166487: Small clusters of intense storms moved northeastward along a surface warm front during the early evening. These storms were associated with a strengthening low-level jet and some cooling aloft. Despite very weak instability, isolated damaging winds occurred in extreme southeast Illinois.
episodes.166488: Two rounds of thunderstorms affected the region. The first round was during the evening, when small clusters of intense storms moved northeastward, producing isolated hail up to the size of nickels. These warm frontal storms were associated with a strengthening low-level jet and some cooling aloft. Late in the night, a line of thunderstorms extended along a cold front from southwest Indiana southwest through far southeast Missouri. As the line moved east, a few bowing segments within this line produced strong winds. Instability was  very limited, but strong winds aloft contributed to the production of isolated strong winds.
episodes.166489: Two rounds of thunderstorms affected the region. The first round was during the evening, when small clusters of intense storms moved northeastward, producing isolated damaging wind events. These warm frontal storms were associated with a strengthening low-level jet and some cooling aloft. Late in the night, a line of thunderstorms extended along a cold front from southwest Indiana southwest through far southeast Missouri. As the line moved east, a few bowing segments within this line produced strong winds. Instability was  very limited, but strong winds aloft contributed to the production of isolated strong winds.
episodes.166490: Small clusters of intense storms moved northeastward during the late afternoon and early evening. These pre-frontal storms were associated with a strengthening low-level jet and some cooling aloft. A surface warm front along the Arkansas border enhanced wind shear, contributing to an isolated very brief tornado despite weak instability.
episodes.167192: At the surface, a front was oriented from southwest to northeast across the state which would help focus the severe weather threat across northern Arkansas. As the upper level storm system moved closer to the area, severe storms developed during the afternoon of March 6th through the morning of the 7th. One main supercell thunderstorm travelled from southeast Johnson County to Randolph County and was responsible for multiple tornadoes through the evening of March 6th. Some additional storms produced mainly weak tornadoes that evening into the early morning hours of the 7th.
episodes.167254: A line of severe thunderstorms with damaging winds pushed through eastern New York during the evening hours of March 7, 2022 resulting in numerous reports of downed trees and power lines. Behind the storms, high winds continued during the late evening of the 7th into the early morning hours of the 8th. Some gusts of 50 to 55 miles per hour were recorded, which resulted in additional downed trees and power lines. Around 13,000 customers lost power in the Albany area, 700 in the Mohawk Valley, 3,000 in the Glens Falls area, and 21,000 in the Mid-Hudson Valley and Catskills. Two schools in the Catskills were closed the following day due to power outages.
episodes.167317: An upper-level disturbance and associated cold front pushed into the Mid-South during the early morning hours of March 7, 2022.  The cold front interacted with a moist and unstable airmass and a line of thunderstorms developed across western Arkansas. The line pushed east into the Mid-South resulting in a few large hail and damaging wind reports.
episodes.167318: An upper-level disturbance and associated cold front pushed into the Mid-South during the early morning hours of March 7, 2022.  The cold front interacted with a moist and unstable airmass and a line of thunderstorms developed across western Arkansas. The line pushed east into the Mid-South resulting in a few large hail and damaging wind reports.
episodes.167492: Deepening surface low pressure lifted across the Upper Ohio Valley during the late morning and afternoon hours of March 7th. An associated cold front swept across the region, with strong cold advection and surface pressure falls contributing to the downward transport of strong wind aloft to the surface.  This manifested as a band of low-topped convective showers along the front, which quickly moved from west to east across the region. Numerous reports of high measured gusts and wind damage were received.  The 62 MPH gust recorded at Pittsburgh International Airport was the sixth-highest gust in the airport's recorded history.
episodes.167598: Early in the morning on March 7th, a cold front dropped south through southern Indiana. This caused localized storm damage in Dubois County.
episodes.167770: An area of low pressure tracking along a nearly stationary frontal boundary brought showers and thunderstorms to southeast Illinois during the evening of March 6th.  One of the thunderstorm cells became severe across Crawford County, causing significant wind damage near Duncanville.
episodes.167898: Some river flooding occurred across western Wisconsin in early March following a rainfall event. Up to 1.5 inches of rain fell and with the ground still frozen, the increased runoff caused flooding to occur along the Trempealeau River.

This tornado started in the southeast corner of Searcy county. The tornado uprooted several trees along its path, along with ripping roof panels off of a barn, and damaging others. It tracked northeast for 0.8 miles in Searcy county.

This tornado started in central Izard county, just southeast of Melbourne, and tracked northeast 9.86 miles in Izard county. The tornado continued into into western Sharp county and dissipating northwest of Evening Shade. There was mostly tree damage. Several homes in and around Sage had roof damage, with a few barns and sheds heavily damaged. The worst damage was 0.5 mile east of Sage, with numerous trees snapped and a horse barn destroyed. Farther northeast, a mobile home was rolled, and a person was injured. A modular home was ripped apart about 4.0 miles west-northwest of Evening Shade. The occupants went to a nearby metal storage container for shelter, and it was rolled. There were four injuries reported here, including one serious injury.

This tornado started in central Izard county, just southeast of Melbourne, and tracked northeast 9.86 miles in Izard county and 1.48 miles in Sharp county. The tornado continued into into western Sharp county and dissipated northwest of Evening Shade. There was mostly tree damage. Several homes in and around Sage had roof damage, with a few barns and sheds heavily damaged. The worst damage was 0.5 mile east of Sage, with numerous trees snapped and a horse barn destroyed. Farther northeast, a mobile home was rolled, and a person was injured. A modular home was ripped apart about 4.0 miles west-northwest of Evening Shade. The occupants went to a nearby metal storage container for shelter, and it was rolled. There were four injuries reported here, including one serious injury.
High water flowed over Doc Bailey Road.

A weather service storm survey found scattered thunderstorm wind damage in an area three to five miles north of Golconda along Highway 146. A manufactured home had most of its roofing material removed. A small portion of roofing was blown off a metal barn. A few small tree limbs were down. Peak winds were estimated between 70 and 75 mph.
Trained storm spotter reported a 62 mph wind gust and trees and power lines down at the junction of Hwy. 167 and Bear Valley Rd. about 5 miles north of Evening Shade.
Several power poles were knocked down along with damage to poultry houses and two structures.
Quarter sized hail was reported.

This tornado started southeast of Dalton in Randolph County. Several small outbuildings were destroyed, there were softwood, shallow rooted trees uprooted, and there were chicken coops that were either completely or partially destroyed. The tornado track was determined by geotagged photos.
Penny sized hail was reported via MPing.

Thunderstorm wind damage consistent with straight line winds during a brief downburst.  The line of thunderstorms produced a very brief bowing segment around 1208 am EST from just south of Merom to just north of County Road 625 South.  Assessment of damage shows property and debris thrown in a generally eastward direction with little or no lofting of debris noted.||Thunderstorm winds blew over a recreational vehicle into a pick-up truck at 5151 West County Road 400 South.  This impact rolled the truck upside down.  Walls of a pole barn were compromised and blown out.  HVAC compressor next to the adjacent house was blown off its platform although essentially no damage occurred to house.  The yard showed no signs of swirls.  Local resident also reported on social media that trees and power lines were also down.  Debris from other damage was also reported in the road 1.75 mile to the WSW at Indiana Route 58 and County Road 450 South.

Thunderstorm winds that may have been a very localized microburst at Indian Creek High School moved a van east of its original location and rolled an empty trailer several hundred yards.  No damage to nearby structures or buses in parking lot.
Tree damage caused by thunderstorm wind gusts on Ford Ridge Road.
Thunderstorm winds blew off shingles and broke 1 inch tree limbs.
A heavy wooden swing set was blown over and thrown through a fence into a field.

This tornado began in western Lincoln county, just south of Glendale, and tracked east-northeast for about 9 miles before dissipating over U.S. Hwy 425, just south of Yorktown. The tornado initially damaged some poultry houses near the start of the path, with the rest of the damage limited to trees.
Several trees were blown over with minor roof damage at County Road 850 South at 350 East.  Four to six nearby telephone poles were snapped at ground level.  Everything fell to the east.
Thunderstorm winds blew over large tree.

This tornado started in southwest Arkansas county , or just west of Lumsdens Reservoir, and tracked northeast for 7 miles, moving along Jacobs Lake, and dissipating just before U.S. Hwy 165, in between Dewitt and Gillett. The primary damage was to trees along this path. Limited access to portions of the track was noted due to nearby lake and property access.
A tree was in the roadway at State Road 56 and 500 West.
A few trees were downed along Williams Road.

Thunderstorm winds caused extensive damage from near Courtland into west side of Seymour with everything blown to the east.  A metal storage barn had sheet metal ripped off and many trees were blown down.
Three power poles were knocked down on Highway 316 one mile north of Highway 49. One tree was also knocked down along with tree limbs.
County Road O-420 at Jones Creek was flooded and impassable.

Up to 1.5 inches of rain fell across the area in early March. With the ground still frozen, the resulting runoff pushed the Trempealeau River out of its banks in Arcadia. The river crested just over the flood stage at 8.15 feet.
Numerous trees were downed across much of Ripley County, especially in the Holton, Osgood, Versailles and Milan areas.

The first tornadic damage was observed along U.S. Route 421 near Jan-Cen-Del Community Schools and extended northeast and then east before dissipating just north of State Road 350, just west of Finks Road. There were several areas that sustained straight line wind damage of similar wind magnitude outside of this path.||The first notable damage was broken tree branches and chimney damage along U.S. Highway 421 just west of the school. The tornado caused roof damage at the school and damaged other light objects around the school. A light pole in the athletic fields north of the school was also knocked down. Blowing debris also caused damage to some buses parked at the school.||Further east, the tornado traveled just north of State Route 350, where additional trees were either uprooted or snapped. Snapped trees resulted in substantial damage to an outbuilding in the 700 block of West State Route 350.||While additional damage of similar strength was observed along West Fairground Road and other locations to the north and east of Osgood, this damage was attributed to wind damage from the line of strong storms that swept through the area at the same time as the tornado.
